terms.definition: The name of the tool proposed in the paper, short for Graph of AI Ideas. It builds a knowledge graph of papers and uses an LLM to search it for trends, learning paths and idea feedback.

A data structure that stores information as nodes (things) connected by labelled edges (relations between them). Here the nodes are papers and prerequisite knowledge, and the edges are citations with semantic labels.
A neural network trained on large amounts of text that can read and write natural language. In this paper LLMs summarize, choose graph paths, and generate ideas through prompts.
Research ideas the LLM generates from a path through the graph, giving a motivation, novelty and method. They are used to check how plausible a path is and to inspire students.
The role a citation plays, such as building on, comparing with or criticizing the cited paper, as opposed to the mere fact that a citation exists.
An existing method that a new method is compared against and aims to surpass.
A neural network that works on graph-structured data by passing information between connected nodes.
A technique where relevant information is looked up and placed in the prompt so the language model can use it when answering.
The top-ranked papers retrieved for a topic, which serve as the starting points from which GoAI grows the graph.
A measure of how similar two vectors are, based on the angle between them. It is commonly used to compare text representations; here it ranks candidate papers against the topic and abstract.
Big-O notation giving how the number of retrieved papers grows with K papers kept per step and N steps in each of two directions.
A citation label meaning the paper builds on, extends, applies or is inspired by the cited paper.
A citation label meaning the paper supports or supplements the cited work through citation, reuse or indirect connection.
A citation label meaning the paper compares itself with the cited paper or proposes an alternative to it.
A citation label meaning the paper questions, corrects or refutes the cited paper. Despite the letters, it does not mean question and answer here.
A citation label for cases where the paper only mentions the cited work or has little direct relevance to it.
A tool that extracts text and paragraphs from scientific PDF files, used here before the LLM labels citations.
A search method that keeps only the best N partial candidates at each step instead of exploring everything. Here N is the beam width and the candidates are paths through the graph.
A prior approach (abbreviated ToG) in which an LLM explores a knowledge graph step by step, choosing relations and then entities. GoAI adopts its two-step strategy.
A reasoning method for language models, used in the paper as the example key reference in its Figure 2 workflow.
A way of prompting a language model to reason through intermediate steps before giving an answer. It is also the name of a paper that appears as a node in the paper's example graph.
A method for improving language-model reasoning by sampling several reasoning paths and combining their answers. It appears as a neighbour of Tree of Thoughts in the paper's example.
A paper that appears as a node in the example graph. The paper does not spell out the acronym.
The summarized development trajectory the LLM produces by evaluating the papers along a path.
The paper's fine-tuned evaluation model that scores the novelty of an idea through three tagged stages: summary, analysis and scoring.
A public platform where conference submissions and their peer-review comments are posted. The paper scrapes it to build training data.
A fine-tuning method that trains only small added low-rank matrices instead of all of a model's weights. The rank controls how small these additions are.
Further trained on a specific dataset so that a pre-trained model adapts to a particular task.
The paper's demonstration application in which students get trends and learning paths, propose ideas, and receive reviewer feedback.
A statistic from -1 to 1 measuring how closely two sets of numbers move together in a linear way. Values near 0 mean little relationship.
An experimental design where each participant is assigned to only one condition, and conditions are compared across different people.
One of the study tasks: drafting a one-page summary of the state of a field, including baselines, extensions, contrasts, datasets/tools and prerequisite knowledge.
The study's second task: proposing one or two project ideas related to the assigned topic.
A standard questionnaire that rates how easy a system is to use, scored out of 100 with higher meaning better usability.
A standard questionnaire that measures perceived workload across subscales such as mental, physical and temporal demand, performance, effort and frustration. Lower scores mean lower load.
